facts.fact: Government and OeSD International signed in April 2026 a concession for a digital civil registry and vital statistics system (NIDCRVS), submitted to the Legislature on 15 July 2026 and before Senate committees since October 2026.

The article says Liberia's Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act was approved in March 2026 and now sets legal standards for handling such data; commencement is not stated.

facts.fact: The National Identification Registry had enrolled about 759,000 people by June 2025, though card issuance was suspended that month, per the article.

The April 2026 concession's plan contemplates ID verification for banking, health, passports, land, business registration and telecoms, with a US$36 fee per bank-account identity check listed in OeSD's annex.

LBR.note: Land registration is named only as a future ID verification use.

facts.fact: Government signed in April 2026 a build-operate-transfer concession with Austria-based OeSD International for a nationwide ID and civil registration system, estimated at US$52 million, still awaiting legislative approval.
